newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt to seek 50pct Duesseldorf airport stake.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt to seek 50pct Duesseldorf airport stake.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt AG (FAG), owner and manager of Frankfurt airport, said it will bid for the 50 percent stake in Duesseldorf airport now held by the North Rhine Westphalia state government.

FAG chairman Wilhelm Bender told a news conference that an offer would be made by a June 4 deadline. He declined to put a value on the stake but said private capital could be needed to finance the purchase.
The other 50 percent is held by the city of Duesseldorf.
FAG wanted to ensure that foreign competitors such as Amsterdam, BAA Plc, Aeroports de Paris or Vienna airport did not gain a foothold in the German airport market, Bender said.
"I do not exclude the fact that foreign competitors are ready to pay a significant sum to get a stake in the German market," he added.
An FAG stake could be a first step towards setting up a German airports system, or "Deutsche Flughaefen AG," Bender said.
It would be a blow to plans for such a network if a company which did not want to join the system took over Duesseldorf, he added.
Some 10 percent of Frankfurt's near-40 million passengers a year came from North Rhine Westphalia and FAG did not intend to lose them to Amsterdam, he said.
Karl Starzacher, finance minister of the state of Hesse, which holds a 45 percent stake in FAG, said a supervisory board meeting on June 2 would discuss the Duesseldorf bid before it was issued.
"There needs to be a broad discussion on whether private capital is needed to make this possible." he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax: 5017
